text:
Predicates:
GrowthStock(x) ::: x is a growth stock.
MatureStock(x) ::: x is a mature stock.
RetirementFund(x) ::: x is suitable for a retirement fund.
Profit(x, y) ::: x is bought to earn profits from y.
Premises:
∀x (GrowthStock(x) → Profit(x, rapidPriceAppreciation)) ::: All growth stocks are bought to earn profits from rapid price appreciation.
∀x (Profit(x, rapidPriceAppreciation) → ¬RetirementFund(x)) ::: If a stock is bought to earn profits from rapid price appreciation, then it is not suitable for a retirement fund.
∃x (GrowthStock(x)) ::: Some stocks are growth stocks.
∀x (MatureStock(x) → RetirementFund(x)) ::: All mature stocks are suitable for a retirement fund.
MatureStock(ko) ::: KO is a mature stock.
Conclusion:
MatureStock(ko) ∧ GrowthStock(ko) ::: KO is a stock and a growth stock.
